changelog: This unit's update source was still pointing at an old address, which is why it could not see any newer versions. It has been repointed at the live update service. Please restart Home Assistant (Settings > System > Restart), then press Check for Update again -- the latest version will be offered.
details: test-branch rescue release, v13: same repair as v12, generalised from one known-bad address to any non-main one. v12 only recognised .../ComfortHA-yaml/test/manifest.json; v13 rewrites CYTECH_MANIFEST_URL to .../ComfortHA-yaml/main/manifest.json whenever the value is this repo on raw.githubusercontent.com and its ref is anything other than main -- the retired test branch, a release tag left behind by a service visit (e.g. .../48a/manifest.json), a commit SHA, or no ref at all. Those all strand the unit, in one of two ways (both reproduced on the bench 2026-09-22): the retired test branch freezes it at v11 while truthfully reporting 'up to date', and a tag- or SHA-pinned URL leaves it reading one frozen manifest forever -- the check offers nothing newer, and if a newer version is offered from that ref the download 404s because cytech_update.sh builds its base URL from a /main/manifest.json suffix, so the owner sees 'Update failed while downloading <file>. Will retry on next boot.' (verified with URL .../48/manifest.json on a v47 unit) and the version never moves. Anything else -- a local mirror, another repo, an unrecognised URL shape, a nested path -- is left strictly alone, so this cannot hijack a unit pointed at a deliberate source. Backup .cytech_secrets.bak_pre_v13_rescue, written once and never overwritten, so the original value survives repeated runs. Ships first_boot.sh (repairs at boot) and cytech_check_only.sh (repairs on Check for Update), function byte-identical in both; either owner action unblocks the unit in one step. Deliberately no git_tag and no dashboard JSONs: the on-disk update script then falls back to the branch URL, and no Core restart or dashboard write is triggered. Units already on /main never see this manifest, and units already repaired by v12 see it as a no-op (their URL is already main).
